correctness.rationale: A direct Peirce-Schur elimination in the incidence algebra proves regularity iff the zero-diagonal complementary Schur block vanishes. The radical is nilpotent, so its only regular element is zero. Free field coordinates count regular elements; support idempotents count inner, reflexive and invertible-inner fibers, and matrix rank versus diagonal zero multiplicity proves a unique commuting group inverse. A graph edge inclusion-exclusion establishes the asymptotic coefficient. All formulas and group-inverse uniqueness have also passed exhaustive small finite-algebra tests, including a genuine order-four field.

value.rationale: Rather than counting all matrix or algebra elements, the result classifies three distinct natural inverse-map fiber sizes for every regular element of every finite incidence algebra, producing exact semigroup statistics indexed by natural diagonal supports. Its regular-element polynomial is unexpectedly invariant under reorientation preserving the comparability graph, with wedge/triangle asymptotic correction; a height-two star/fence pair with equal algebra dimension is distinguished both by regular-element and reflexive-inverse counts.
